messages:
Kai: Heads-up: saw a decode perf regression after the fused-attn/paged change. Small-batch chat p95 is higher on g5.
Samir: Which scenario? long prefill + decode or short-turn streaming? 
Kai: Short-turn streaming. Batch sizes 1-4, KV cache on. Prefill numbers look stable, decode is where kernel choice seems to regress.
Maya: Can you drop the microbench results?
perf-bot: ```
Benchmark VM: g5.x8 | model: valkyrie-7b | prefill_seq=512 decode_seq=64
- prefill p95: 340 ms
- decode p95 (batch=1): baseline 28 ms -> after patch 33 ms (+17.8%)
- decode p95 (batch=4): baseline 60 ms -> after patch 68 ms (+13.3%)
Hotspots: fused_attention_kernel (decode) accounts for ~45% CPU time; observed queued kernel launches and memcpy spikes.
```
Olivia: memcpy spikes suggest KV layout or page copy behavior changed. Does the paged flow add an extra copy for small seqs?
Samir: The paged-attn patch introduced a pageswap step that staggers KV copies across pages. Good for long prefill (amortized), bad for tiny decode steps where the copies happen each token.
Kai: Exactly. Prefill is a big continuous batch so the paged/fused path amortizes overhead. Decode often has single-token steps and we keep hitting page-swap overhead.
Maya: Quick test: force the kernel selector to avoid paged decode for small decode lengths. Kai, can you run with a kernel-policy override and report batch=1?
Samir: Running command: 
```
./runtime --model valkyrie-7b --seq-prefill 512 --seq-decode 64 --batch 1 --kernel-policy "no-paged-decode"
```
perf-bot: ```
Result: decode p95 (batch=1) -> 29 ms (back to baseline).
Note: forcing non-paged fused-simple path reduced memcpy activity.
```
Olivia: That's a strong signal: selector heuristics need to be data-aware. Prefer simpler fused path for decode when seq_decode is small. Also consider micro-batching debounce to group consecutive decode tokens when latency policy allows.
Kai: Other angle: KV cache residency. If we keep the last N pages resident for active sessions, page swaps would drop and decode would avoid repeated memcpy.
Maya: Memory tradeoff though. If we increase resident pages per-session, high concurrency could blow memory. Need safe bounds and per-tenant caps.
Samir: Proposal: adaptive resident_pages = max(1, min(8, floor(reserved_gb / 8))). That ties residency to reserved capacity.
Olivia: Also add a perf counter: page_swap_events_per_token and expose it in Console route metrics. That will help correlate customer regressions to churn.
Kai: Agreed. Action items:
- Samir: add kernel-selector rule: avoid paged decode when seq_decode < 128. Put PR up and run canary. :white_check_mark:
- Maya: implement page-swap perf counter and dashboard chart. Tracked in ticket ENGRT-4621. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
- Olivia: prototype resident-pages heuristic with safety caps and OOM guard. :rocket:
- Kai: add unit test to kselector simulating alternating prefill+token decode steps so future fused/paged patches don't regress decode.
Maya: One more test: rerun fused-attn microbench with CUDA mempools disabled; pooling can hide memcpy patterns and we need a clear signal.
Samir: I'll run the A/B on canary with the new selector. If prefill stays stable and decode improves, we'll roll. Also will collect page_swap_events_per_token.
Kai: Thanks. If we still see issues, consider adding a lightweight decode-only kernel path that uses in-place KV pointers (no page copy) for batch <= 2.
Olivia: Noted. Also document the selector heuristics and perf counters in the eng-runtime README so oncall can triage.
Maya: Thanks team. Filing follow-ups and linking perf traces.
Kai: Cheers.
